fig1_delay_overview: Boston MBTA bus, real actual vs scheduled times. 4,606,471 departure events on 'Schedule'-standard trips (4 sampled months of 2024). On time = -1 to +5 min of schedule. Headway panel uses 'Headway'-standard trips: bunched = actual gap under half the scheduled gap.
fig2_delay_routes_and_buildup: Boston MBTA bus, real actual vs scheduled times. Routes ranked need at least 100 events. Right: mean delay at the 1st, 2nd... timepoint of a trip (first 15 timepoints); the curve is not monotonic and later timepoints cover far fewer trips.
fig3_actual_vs_scheduled_slowdown: Boston MBTA bus, real actual vs scheduled times. Each point is a segment between consecutive timepoints of a route and direction with at least 100 peak and off-peak events (1,442 segments). Points near the dashed line mean the timetable already plans the slowdown that really happens.
fig4_completeness_waterfall: Boston MBTA bus, real actual vs scheduled times. Rows after each stage (percentage = share of the previous stage kept). 'quality' = defects (missing actual time, duplicates, implausible delay); 'scope' = Headway-standard trips are intentionally excluded from the delay analysis and the model.
fig5_ml_regression: Boston MBTA bus, real actual vs scheduled times. Trained on 1,001,114 events of the training days, evaluated on 1,226,518 events of held-out days (last 25% of each month). GBT test R2 = 0.80, RMSE = 2.92 min.
fig6_ml_classification: Boston MBTA bus, real actual vs scheduled times. Held-out test days only (1,226,518 events). Accuracy 89.4%, AUC 0.946; threshold 0.5 on the predicted probability. 'Never late' is the majority-class baseline.
fig7_ml_feature_importance: Boston MBTA bus, real actual vs scheduled times. Importances of the full-feature GBT models (Spark MLlib featureImportances). A high importance shows the model relies on a feature, not that it causes delay.
fig8_pipeline_speedup: Boston MBTA bus, real actual vs scheduled times: 8,424,946 cleaned events from months [1, 4, 7, 10]. 1 timed run(s) after 0 discarded warm-up; each core count in its own process. Machine: Apple M3, 8 logical cores (4 performance + 4 efficiency), 16.0 GB.
fig9_model_training_speedup: Boston MBTA bus, real actual vs scheduled times: 1,001,114 training rows, 40 boosting rounds, depth 5. Median of 1 timed run(s) after 0 discarded warm-up; each core count in its own process.
